title: Silent Alarm: A J-Space Protocol for Comparing Danger Recognition Across Models and Quantization Levels
abstract: arXiv:2607.12792v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Jailbreak-robustness research typically evaluates safety through generated responses using an LLM-as-judge approach. Such evaluations, however, are sensitive to the benchmark's grading procedure and capture only observed behavior on a given set of attacks, without directly revealing the hidden fragility of the underlying safety mechanisms. This work proposes JADR (Jacobian Assessment of Danger Recognition), a protocol that measures a model's internal representation through Jacobian space (J-space, a recently proposed workspace of verbalizable concepts) before the first response token is generated. translated_title: 静默警报：一种用于跨模型和量化级别比较危险识别的J-Space协议
translated_abstract: arXiv:2607.12792v2 公告类型：替换-交叉 摘要：越狱鲁棒性研究通常通过使用LLM作为评判者的方法，基于生成的响应来评估安全性。然而，这类评估对基准的评分过程敏感，且仅捕获在给定攻击集上观察到的行为，无法直接揭示底层安全机制的隐藏脆弱性。本研究提出了JADR（雅可比危险识别评估），一种通过雅可比空间（J-space，一种最近提出的可言语化概念工作空间）在生成首个响应令牌之前测量模型内部表示的协议。对于每个提示和层，我们记录前k个J-space令牌；这些令牌被分组到六个行为场景轴中，并基于StrongREJECT的危险样本与基于XSTest和OKTest的安全对照组进行比较。该方法不调用外部评判模型：计算完全在本地运行，基于模型的激活值进行。
tldr: 提出一种无需外部评判模型、在响应生成前通过雅可比空间内部表示测量模型危险识别能力的协议，用于跨模型和量化级别比较安全性。
en_tdlr: Proposes a protocol that measures a model's danger recognition via Jacobian-space internal representations before response generation, requiring no external judge, for comparing safety across models and quantization levels.
